title: feat(desktop): renaming an item renames its file, so users find it in the folder (NIW2-560)
body:
Renaming an item in the library now renames its file in the vault folder, so the name a user types is the name they find in Finder or Explorer. New captures also start with readable names (`Kaipu Recording 2026-10-29 at 13.51.00`, `Kaipu Screenshot …`, `Kaipu GIF …`) instead of `recording-2026-10-29-13-51-00` / `screenshot-2026-10-29T…Z`.

**Why.** Until now `rename()` only wrote `title` into `.kaipu/<id>.json`; the file kept its first name. A user who renamed an item to "Updated name" and opened the folder could not find it, which reads as a lost file, especially for Windows users. The vault keyed everything on the filename ("the filename is the id") from the first recorder commit, with no ADR. Routes, cloud, tags and export provenance have since moved to `assetId`, which made the move feasible. Ticket: [NIW2-560](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-560/renaming-a-library-item-renames-its-file-on-disk-with-readable-default). Spec: `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/specs/2026-10-29-niw2-560-rename-renames-the-file.md`. Decision: ADR 0032 (`architecture/decisions/0032-the-file-name-follows-the-title.mdx`, status Proposed, implemented on this branch; it is accepted only after owner QA and the Windows steps below).

How a rename works now (`LibraryVault.renameItem`):

1. Under a vault-wide names lock, resolve the item **by `assetId`**, never by a bare id. A stale id (for example a toast's Retry) follows the item; an identity that two files claim is refused.
2. Save the title first, so the user's name is never lost.
3. Derive a stem from the title. It must be valid on Windows and macOS (NFKC, forbidden characters, reserved names, trailing dots/spaces, length budget), must not be a companion-shaped or reserved name (`Demo.edit`, `tags`), and collisions get ` (2)`, compared through a filesystem-style case fold.
4. Copy companions to the new stem (`.json`, `.jpg`, `.cursor.json`, `.edit.json`, `.edit.meta.json`, `.assets/`), `fs.rename` the media file (the commit point), then delete the old companions. A crash at any point leaves the old item or the new item whole.
5. If the file is locked (EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES after 3 retries), an export is running, or the item is open in the video editor, the title is saved, the file keeps its old name, and a toast says why, with Retry where it makes sense.

## What changes for you

- **Renaming an item renames its file** and every `.kaipu/` companion. Before: only the title changed. Existing items keep their current filenames until they are renamed; there is no bulk migration.
- **New captures get readable names**, both the title and the file. Legacy `recording-<iso>` stems display as the new default title (local time).
- **A rename can keep the old filename**, with a toast. This happens when another app holds the file, an export is running, the item is open in the video editor, or two files in the folder claim the same item. The title is always saved.
- **Video editor:** if its item disappeared or is claimed twice, it shows a "no longer available" or "claimed twice" state with Back to Library. It no longer opens the route's id.
- **IPC contract:** the rename is now `renameLocalRecording(id, assetId, title)`, which requires `assetId` and returns a `RenameResult` (new id, file outcome, reason). The screenshot overwrite requires `overwriteAssetId`. The new channels `library:editor-session-acquire` and `-close` exist. All are documented in `desktop/ipc-contract.mdx`.
- **`kaipu-media://` URLs percent-encode the id** through `shared/media-url.ts`, and the handler answers 400 to a malformed escape or a traversal attempt.
- **Fixes that fell out of the work:**
  - Two screenshots taken in the same second no longer overwrite each other: `allocateId` reserves names.
  - `remove()` now deletes the `.edit.*` files and `.assets/` too.
  - Drag-out names use the same stem rules: spaces instead of `-`, and a 100-character cap instead of 180.

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/library-vault.ts:390` — `renameItem` ordering and outcomes.** Decide whether every early return after step 1 leaves a consistent item, and whether "title saved, file kept" is the right answer to each failure, rather than throwing.
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/library-vault.ts:529` — `resolveIdentity`.** The policy is: the fast path when the caller's id still holds the identity; otherwise exactly one media-bearing stem across all kinds; otherwise refuse. Decide whether refusing an ambiguous identity is the right UX, compared with picking the newest.
3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/file-stem.ts:33` — `fsFold` / `isReservedStem` / `fileStemFromTitle`.** The fold deliberately over-matches (NFKC → lower → upper → lower), so a false match costs a ` (2)` and a missed one could merge two items. Decide whether NFKC in the visible filename is acceptable: `ſ` becomes `s` and fullwidth letters become ASCII.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/editor-sessions.ts:46` and `library-vault.ts:511` — the editor hold.** It is acquired under the names lock, refused when the window went away or reloaded (generation counter), and released on `destroyed`, `render-process-gone` and main-frame navigation. Unit tests use fake windows only; whether Electron delivers those events as expected cannot be judged from the diff.
5. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/default-capture-name.ts:25` — the default name format.** `Kaipu <Kind> YYYY-MM-DD at HH.mm.ss`, local time. Decide whether to keep the `Kaipu ` prefix (spec open question 1, default yes).

**Safe to skim:** docs (`library-vault.mdx`, `ipc-contract.mdx`, the ADR, the spec change log), the i18n en/es pairs, the mechanical caller updates that thread `assetId` through, fixture renames from `Recording — …` to the new default names, and the merge commit from `main`, which only touches CI.

## Proof

| Criterion (NIW2-560) | What was done | How to check it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Renaming an item in the app changes the filename on disk to the sanitized title; the item keeps its assetId, tags, thumbnail, edit project and cursor track. | `renameItem` moves media and all companions under the names lock | `library-vault.rename.test.ts`; manual step 2 | Unit suite green, see Checks. Manual: not verified by me (no Electron launch) |
| Two items with the same title get distinct filenames. | collision suffix ` (2)` via fold-aware `isStemFree` | rename tests "… (2)"; manual step 3 | Unit suite green |
| A rename whose file is locked keeps the new title, keeps the old filename and tells the user. | 3 retries, then `kept-old-name` + toast with Retry | rename tests with an injected EPERM; manual step 6 (Windows) | Unit suite green. **Windows: not verified** |
| New captures are saved under a readable default name. | `defaultCaptureName` + `allocateId` in every writer | `default-capture-name.test.ts`; manual step 1 | Unit suite green |
| Unit tests cover sanitization, collisions, crash ordering and the locked-file path. | test-first per unit; each review finding got a regression test seen failing first | `bun run verify` | exit 0, 3133 tests |

Adversarial review: GPT-6.1 Sol (Codex, high effort) ran 7 rounds; findings went 6 → 3 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 2 → 0. Round 7 verdict: *"Clean re-check… Risk: low; safe to merge the reviewed delta."* Topics fixed along the way:
- companion and reserved name overlap (`Demo.edit`, `tags`, and Unicode aliases like `ſ`);
- a screenshot overwrite racing a rename;
- `#` and `%` in media URLs;
- reopened-screenshot bytes;
- the editor hold lifecycle (race, stale owner, crash);
- Retry acting on a stale id;
- ambiguous identities, including across media kinds.

## Decisions

- **The local id stays "filename without extension", and a rename changes it.** Options: keep the filename fixed and only show it in the UI; decouple the id from the filename entirely (id = `assetId`, which needs an index); rename the file. Taken: rename. `list()` stays a `readdir`, the vault stays readable without the app, and cross-item links already use `assetId`.
- **The title stays in the sidecar; the filename is a sanitized projection of it.** A title can hold `: / ? "` or 500 characters; a filename cannot.
- **Ordering: title, copy companions, rename media, delete old companions.** The alternative was to move each file in turn. Copy-first guarantees one whole item at every crash point. Leftovers are invisible to `list()`, and sweeping them is deferred to NIW2-561.
- **A failure keeps the old filename instead of failing the rename.** The title is what the user asked for, and a modal for an invisible OS condition would only confuse.
- **Ambiguous identity is refused, not guessed.** Picking the newest could rename or overwrite the wrong file.
- **NFKC in filenames.** Using NFC plus a fold would keep exotic characters on disk. NFKC removes compatibility characters, so fewer aliases can exist at all.
- **Default names in this PR, not a separate one.** Owner decision.
- **External renames and deletes are out of scope:** [NIW2-561](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-561/reconcile-the-library-with-files-changed-outside-the-app-on-reload).

## Checks

- `bun run verify` → exit 0. kaipu-record: 315 test files, 3133 tests passed. The other packages pass. Typecheck and build are clean. Lint: 0 errors, 17 warnings, all present on `main` before this branch.
- Desktop Playwright E2E was not run locally (ADR 0006); `e2e/library-actions.e2e.ts` now asserts `Renamed Clip.mp4` on disk, and CI runs it.

## Manual verification

- [ ] Steps 1–5 below on macOS
- [ ] Step 6 on Windows (locked file)

## How to test it yourself

Run `bun run dev` from this branch. Open the vault folder in Finder (Settings → Files → open folder), and press Cmd+Shift+. to see `.kaipu/`.

1. **Default name.** Record 5 s.
   - Expect: the Library shows "Kaipu Recording 2026-10-29 at HH.MM.SS", the folder has a `.mp4` with the same name, and `.kaipu/` has its `.json`, `.jpg` and `.cursor.json` under that name.
   - Broken if: you see `recording-2026-…`.
2. **Rename.** Open the item, click the pencil, type `Sprint demo: part 1/2?` and press Enter.
   - Expect: the title keeps its punctuation, the video keeps playing from the same spot, and the tags stay. The file becomes `Sprint demo part 1 2.mp4`, its companions move with it, and nothing named `Kaipu Recording …` is left behind.
   - Broken if: the old file remains, or tags or the thumbnail disappear.
3. **Collision.** Rename another item to the same title.
   - Expect: `Sprint demo part 1 2 (2).mp4` on disk, and no " (2)" in the in-app title.
4. **Screenshots.** Take two screenshots within one second.
   - Expect: two `.png` files, the second ending in ` (2)`. On `main` the second overwrites the first.
   - Then open one in the editor, change its title, edit something and leave. Expect a single `.png` under the new name, with the edits saved.
5. **Busy and editing.**
   - Start a long export from the video editor, then rename the source from the Library. Expect the toast "Name saved. The file keeps its old name while an export is running." with Retry. The export completes, and Retry then renames the file.
   - Separately, open an item in the video editor in one window and rename it from another. Expect the "open in the editor" toast.
6. **Windows, locked file.** Open the `.mp4` in Media Player, then rename it in Kaipu.
   - Expect the "…because another app is using it." toast. Close the player and click Retry: the file is renamed.

## What I did not verify

- **Windows behaviour:** the error codes for a locked file, `fs.rename` over an existing target, and whether our own `kaipu-media://` streams block a rename. These are hypotheses; the retry and the `kept-old-name` outcome cover them either way.
- **Electron window events:** delivery of `destroyed`, `render-process-gone` and `did-start-navigation` to `EditorSessions.watch`. Only fake windows were tested.
- **The app itself:** not launched, and the E2E suite was not run locally. Manual steps 1–6 are for the owner.
- **Case-only renames on a case-sensitive filesystem (ext4):** only unit-tested on APFS.
- **Flaky test:** the reviewer saw the existing discard-modal test fail once and pass on repeat. It is intermittent and not linked to this patch.
